get.description: Indoor tasks are verbal and written; outdoor tasks are physical.
The brief only. The model solution is withheld until a plan is submitted.

Stimuli for a sheet to print and solve on paper.

Practising on paper is how the test is actually sat, and it is also the only
way to rehearse writing at speed by hand. The printed sheet and the upload
below are two halves of the same loop.

post.description: Submit a paper sitting once the transcription has been confirmed.

Read an uploaded answer sheet into an editable draft.

The image is decoded in memory and dropped when the request ends -- it is
never written to disk or to the database. What comes back is a *draft* the
candidate corrects; handwriting recognition is not reliable enough to be
treated as the answer, and the analysis only ever sees confirmed text.

Works without OCR installed: the response then carries empty slots and the
candidate types their answers in, which is still faster than re-sitting.

patch.description:
Role and status changes are super-admin only, and never self-applied.

Letting an admin edit their own row is how an account locks itself out or
quietly promotes itself; both need a second person.

Pull recent stories from the configured public RSS feeds.

Reads syndication feeds -- the format publishers provide for this -- and
stores the headline, summary, source and link. It does not copy any other
site's question bank; with ``generate`` set, questions are written from the
stories by this platform's own pipeline and land in the review queue.

GtoVenue.title: GtoVenue
GtoVenue.description:
Where a GTO task is conducted.

The series splits in two, and candidates prepare for the halves differently:
indoor tasks are verbal and written, judged on how you think and speak, and
they can be rehearsed alone at a desk. Outdoor tasks are physical and
equipment-bound, judged on how you organise a group over an obstacle.

Sources disagree about where the planning exercise belongs -- it uses a
sand model or sketch map and is sometimes run under a shade outside. It is
filed as indoor here because nothing about it is physical: it is written
individually, then discussed and presented, which is the indoor pattern.

PpdtPerception.title: PpdtPerception
PpdtPerception.description:
The proforma a candidate fills before writing the story.

Screening day asks for the number of characters, then age, sex, mood and
action for the main one -- and the story has to agree with what was written
here. That consistency is half of what is being assessed, so it is captured
as structure rather than buried in prose.

TranscriptionOut.title: TranscriptionOut
TranscriptionOut.description:
The draft reading of an uploaded sheet, for the candidate to correct.

``slots`` is the transcription already aligned to the sitting's items, which
is what the correction form binds to. Anything the reader could not place is
left empty rather than guessed -- a misplaced line would attribute words to
the wrong stimulus, and the candidate could not tell from the result.
